# Independent audit of the symmetric truncation energy inequality

Audited Sections1--2 of
`candidate 2be89ee8039bb5fd`.
Result: PASS. No correction requested.

The layer-cake weights 2r dh/M form a probability measure on uniform
centered intervals. Their captured fractions are (1+x)/2 with
x=min(T/r,1), so E x=2v-1. For r<T the full-layer integral is
1/[1-(kr/T)^2]<=1/(1-k^2)=I_k(1). Polynomial division gives

    I_k(x)=(x+1-k)/(2(1-k))-k/(2(x+k)),

so I_k''=-k/(x+k)^3 exactly. Jensen and the stated substitution give the
claimed p=2 bound. The exponent comparison is valid for negative as well
as positive a: log(1+t)-t/(1+t)>=0 for every t>-1, with equality only at0.
All denominators remain positive on the entire captured support because
c_p<0 and s<=T.

The projected density of a centrally symmetric convex body is even and
unimodal by actual section inclusion and Brunn--Minkowski (uniform in
dimension1). The symmetric-slab lower bound follows directly from Jensen.
Combining the upper energy bound with the cap fraction gives exactly

    v^2/(3v-1)-4/9=(3v-2)^2/[9(3v-1)].

The stated one-dimensional sharpness and higher-dimensional strictness
under a proper cut also check. This audit does not supply a general-body
reduction to the later pyramid application.

The later Section5 arbitrary-stationary-menu extension was checked as
well. From 2v-1<=e<=(2v-1)/v one gets
1/(2-e)<=v<=(1+e)/2. Its lower affine bound factors as

    1/(2-e)-4e/9-4/9=(2e-1)^2/[9(2-e)]>=0,

and the upper is 1/2+e/18<=5/9. The displayed cap/coarea identity therefore
puts p-[(p0-4/9)/C0]C in [4/9,5/9] for each apex cap. Reversal complements
p and negates the signed vertical coarea, preserving the same interval.
Vertical caps have half volume by central symmetry of every horizontal
section. Actual vertical coarea balance cancels the correction for any
stationary menu, with no orbit hypothesis. This extension also passes.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
